content: 6 min read 2 hours ago -- Press enter or click to view image in full size Your app is not slow because your business logic is heavy. It is slow because of a hundred small, invisible decisions made by whatever rendered the page before your logic even ran. I spent years treating directives as a syntax detail, something Angular provides so templates can conditionally show a div. Then I found six directives, some built in, some fifteen lines of my own code, that quietly did more for real user-perceived speed than any algorithm I ever optimized. None of these require a rewrite. Every one of them drops directly into an existing template. Let us walk through what each one actually buys you, with the numbers to prove it. Directive 1: NgOptimizedImage, Angular’s Own Answer to Slow Images The problem Images are, on almost every real website, the single heaviest thing on the page, and the plain tag gives the browser almost no help prioritizing them correctly. Nothing here tells the browser this image matters early, nothing sets explicit dimensions to prevent layout shift, and nothing lazy loads the images further down the page…
